Messages.Author: Michael S Phillips
Messages.Body:
Why do you need three dominate master cards if you only have five cards
requiring that skill (gov the un.)? My advice would be either get rid of all
but one of the masters or include some other minor helpful dominate cards,
especially defelction, obedience, grave robbing, etc. Bleed bounce has always
worked well in my vote decks, I would also recommend adding tel. misdirections,
if any of your vamps has superior auspex (I can't remember off-hand). Overall
this looks like a good deck even though it is huge. . .a fragment of the book
of nod would help you cycle through your cards quicker (if you have one that
is) Let us know how your crazy votin' deck fares, huh?

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Mark Havener <elfh...@netcom.com> wrote:
>On a related note: Can a Hellhound receive equipment from another minion
>via the Heidelburg Castle? This would seem to be a loophole that could
>be used to give equipment to the Hound, which could have easily been
>soved by just writing "the Hellhound cannot have equipment"on the
>Hellhound card...

Yes, hellhounds can receive equipment via Heidelburg Castle. They can
also receive equipment via playing Zip Gun. Basically, the intention was not

to let hellhounds have equipment, ever. It was just that they couldn't
take actions: they couldn't do D-bleeds, couldn't go after cards that let
themselves be burned as actions (like Pentex Subversion), and so on. Being
"unable" to have equipment is simply the most visible result of being unable
to take actions.

Agreed. Although WotC's lack of concern for its customers in general
makes me angry, Tom is (no offense) naught but a messenger of them here.
He tells us what the rules team does or what other sections of WotC is
doing [even if he does have some part in it]. He does not deserve this
treatment. I think a lot of people take for granted the fact that he is
here at all. WotC doesn't HAVE to have a netrep for this topic,
especially considering that J/VTES isn't their best-selling game.
I'm not saying that everyone should lep up and shake Tom's hand for
what he does, especially when he doesn't seem to care about what would
seem like an insignificant detail but actually has an impact on the game
[case in point:Disguised Weapon discussions recently], but cut the man
some slack folks. I'm good with cards, but Tom probably has to keep track
of so many [probably all the magic cards with errata, plus all the VTES
cards, and their old Jyhd counterparts and all THEIR errata], that it's
no wonder he makes a mistake now and then. Hell, a group of us played
with Dark Sovereigns for almost a week without ever noticing that you
couldn't use Heidelburg Castle on a vamp in torpor. Nobody's perfect.

I'm sorry that you thought that my post was a "harsh" response. Could you
explain how either of my two sentences convey a sense of malice? I have
seen malicious posts on this group... I do not believe that mine was one
of them. I like Jyhad. And I do like the fact that Tom does pass along
information from the official source. You will note that I do NOT complain
about the game, or the company. I do NOT complain about Tom's involvement
in this group. All I said were two things:

Looks like he forgot how to spell.

speaking as a member of a small community. I affirmed this fact in a non
accusatory way.

I too feel that Tom (and WoTC) takes quite a bit of abuse on this group, and
it is not fair for us to berate Tom for taking time to help us out and to do
his job in the best way he knows how. But if there are _valid_ concerns,
and _valid_ arguments, why can we not voice them?

I do NOT appreciate your singling my post out as abusive from a cast of
thousands which actually had that intent.

-James

>myself. I was under the impression that a Minion referred to ALL
>creatures, vamps or otherwise. And what is the difference between an
>Ally and a Retainer?

>-BUZZ
>[DISCLAIMER: the opinion(s) expressed in this article are entirely
>that of the poster, and in no way reflect that of The Walt Disney
>Company.]

Minions does indeed refer to vampires and allies. Basically
independant entities capable of taking actions and/or blocking.
Ally is a minion recruited by a vampire that is controlled by the
Meth.
Retainers are recruited by a minion and stay attached to the minion.
Retainers cannot act independantly and merlley supply some advantage
or mod to the controling minion.
Rory

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Buzz <philli...@corp.disney.com> wrote:
>> The magazine, I believe, is none other than the most recent Inquest...
>>In that Q&A, the first question asked if allies could get equipment. The
>>answer they gave was [give or take an unimportant word] "No, allies

>>cannot use equipment. Only vampires and minions may use equipment."...

> I am a relatively new player and was somewhat confused about that

>myself...

Probably because their statement is incorrect. All minions can use
equipment, and "minions" includes allies as well as vampires.

>And what is the difference between an Ally and a Retainer?

Basically, allies can function independently (as vampires can), whereas
retainers are always attached to a particular vampire or ally, much
like equipment is.
